title: Jio's ₹10.3 Lakh Crore IPO Tests Whether Cheap Data Can Pay
excerpt: A decade after Jio cut data prices from ₹228 to about ₹7.5 a gigabyte, Jio Platforms opens India's largest IPO on October 21, with anchor bids of more than ₹2.5 lakh crore and a valuation case resting on monetisation, not subscriber growth.
body:
• Jio Platforms opens its IPO on October 21 and closes it on October 23 at a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 a share, valuing the company at about ₹10.3 lakh crore, or roughly $108 billion, at the top end.
  • The ₹30,213 crore issue is entirely a fresh issue with no offer for sale, and up to ₹27,500 crore of the proceeds will repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm.
  • Anchor investors bid more than ₹2.5 lakh crore, about 30 times the anchor tranche, with Life Insurance Corp. of India taking the largest allocation at ₹499.98 crore.
  • For readers weighing the issue: bidding runs October 21-23, shares are expected to list on October 28, and at ₹1,119 the stock is priced at about 33 times fiscal 2026 earnings, so the case rests on rising revenue per user, not subscriber growth alone.

A gigabyte of mobile data in India cost ₹228 a decade ago. Today it costs about ₹7.5. That collapse, engineered by Reliance Jio after its 2016 launch, is the foundation of the investment case now being tested as Jio Platforms seeks a valuation of about ₹10.3 lakh crore in what would be India's largest initial public offering, according to The Economic Times.

The ₹30,213 crore offering would overtake Hyundai Motor India's ₹27,870 crore issue in 2024 as the country's biggest. TechCrunch reported that the sale comprises up to 270 million new shares, with ₹25 billion of shares reserved for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and ₹5 billion for employees at a ₹54 per share discount.

Scale built on cheap data

Jio changed how India accesses the internet, accelerated the shift from voice to data and now carries about 60% of the country's wireless data traffic. Industry download speeds rose from about 2.5 megabits per second when Jio entered the market to more than 68 Mbps by fiscal 2026, while average monthly data use rose from less than 0.2 GB per customer to 26.7 GB, according to a Systematix report cited by The Economic Times. Jio's own customers used 43.7 GB a month in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

Reliance Jio Infocomm had 533.3 million customers as of June 2026, and its wireless broadband network covered more than 99% of India's population. Revenue rose to ₹1,46,885.8 crore in fiscal 2026 from ₹1,28,218.4 crore a year earlier, while EBITDA increased 16.4% to ₹73,382.1 crore and the EBITDA margin improved to 50% from 49.2%, according to Ventura Securities figures cited in the report. Cash flow from operations rose to ₹77,556.3 crore.

Anchor demand passes the first test

On Monday, Jio allotted about 72.5 million shares to 212 anchor investors at ₹1,119 each, raising ₹8,109.85 crore, according to CEOWORLD Magazine. Bids exceeded ₹2.5 lakh crore, roughly 30 times the shares on offer. Domestic mutual funds took 34.34% of the anchor portion through 95 schemes from 25 fund houses, while BlackRock, Fidelity, Capital Group, the Government of Singapore and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority were also among the allottees.

Half of the anchor shares can be sold from November 24 and the rest from January 23, 2027, making those lock-in expiries a cleaner test of conviction.

The valuation depends on monetisation

Average revenue per user rose from ₹181.7 in fiscal 2024 to ₹214 in fiscal 2026 and ₹215.6 in the June 2026 quarter. More than 260 million Indians still use 2G networks, and their migration to smartphones is a large potential market. Jio is also expanding beyond mobile: its fixed broadband base stood at 28.6 million in June, including 14 million JioAirFiber subscribers, and it had 284.9 million 5G customers in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

The pitch extends to cloud, enterprise services, private 5G, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Jio has filed 7,220 patent applications, and its JioBrain AI engine is used for network optimisation. At the upper price band, Jio is valued at around 33 times fiscal 2026 earnings, according to Systematix, which recommended subscribing and pointed to market leadership, profitability and cash generation.

Risks investors are pricing

The company will need continued spending on networks, spectrum and AI infrastructure, and satellite broadband could add competition. It remains heavily dependent on Reliance Jio Infocomm for revenue and profits, and deferred spectrum payment liabilities of about ₹1.05 lakh crore sit outside reported borrowings of ₹70,781 crore at the end of March 2026, according to offer document summaries. Its reported return on net worth of about 9.4% also trails Bharti Airtel's roughly 20%.

The public offer runs from October 21 to October 23, with listing tentatively set for October 28. Lower data prices created the network and rising usage created the audience. The IPO now tests whether 5G, broadband, cloud and AI can turn that audience into a larger earnings stream.
image_caption: The Jio building at Reliance Corporate Park, Navi Mumbai. Jio Platforms, Reliance Jio's parent, opens its IPO on October 21 at a valuation of about ₹10.3 lakh crore.
nri_angle: India's largest IPO is priced at about 33 times fiscal 2026 earnings; NRI and global investors watching Reliance should track ARPU, debt repayment and anchor lock-in expiries rather than subscriber scale alone.
author: Diaspora Desk
